idiom_name: @Observable view-model + @State/@Environment ownership; SwiftUI tracks property reads in body
implementation_notes: SwiftUI plus the Observation framework absorb the pattern: the @Observable macro generates observation at compile time, a view's body creates dependencies only on the properties it actually reads (so unrelated changes do not re-render), and @State/@Environment own and distribute the view-model - no notify calls, no observer base class, no manual subscription. Commands are plain methods the view calls, and derived view state is a computed property tracked through the observable properties it reads. This is the default for iOS 17/macOS 14 and later.
pitfalls: Only properties read inside body are tracked: state read in a helper that body does not execute (or captured once in .task) creates no dependency and never updates.
@Observable classes are reference types: mutating properties off the main actor still mutates UI-visible state - isolate the model or hop to the main actor.
@State owns the model; creating it inside body or as a default in a child view re-creates and loses state - lift it to the owner or use @Environment.
Mixing @Observable types with @ObservedObject/@StateObject keeps working but retains the coarser object-level update behaviour; migrate deliberately.

variants.name: ObservableObject + @Published (Combine)
variants.implementation_notes: The pre-iOS-17 realization: the view-model conforms to ObservableObject, each bound property is @Published (backed by Combine's objectWillChange publisher), and the view holds it with @StateObject (owner), @ObservedObject (borrowed) or @EnvironmentObject. Any published change invalidates views observing the object even if they do not read the changed property - coarser than Observation tracking - and optionals or collections of objects cannot be tracked. Use it for targets older than iOS 17 or code already built on Combine.
pitfalls: @Published belongs on the stored property: applying it to a computed property or the wrong member does not publish, and the view silently stops updating.
@ObservedObject on a value created inside the view (or defaulted) re-creates the view-model on every render; only @StateObject owns it.
Publishing happens on the updating thread; mutating from a background queue drives UI updates off the main thread.
objectWillChange fires before the value is written, so subscribers that read the property immediately see pre-change data.
